rows.responsibility: Call E2EE implementation: temporary/private key lifecycle, one-shot ECDH envelopes, media encrypt/decrypt callback, participant/state blocks, inbound/outbound message queues, subchain reconciliation, timers/failure state and emoji verification hash.
rows.state_machine: generate/import key -> establish call state -> apply participant/state blocks -> encrypt/decrypt messages/media -> reconcile subchains -> expose verification/failure -> destroy keys/teardown
rows.side_effects: Owns ephemeral crypto handles and call-E2EE protocol state; emits encrypted outbound/inbound application effects and verification hash.
rows.failure_cases: invalid key size/public key; ECDH/encrypt/decrypt failure; invalid/out-of-order block; missing call id; subchain timeout/retry; stale participant state; teardown during callbacks; key destruction; replay/duplicate inbound; recovery after reconnect
rows.ui_disposition: Use canonical Call/Participant/Status/Alert/verification surfaces; no Telegram-derived call UI.
rows.fabushi_canonical_owner: Canonical Calls E2EE/Crypto + Call Session owner
rows.platform_differences: td/e2e and MTP bindings are source-specific; preserve E2EE key ownership, forward state application, replay/order handling, verification UX and teardown in canonical call crypto/session owners.
rows.production_evidence: Exact accepted blob read; canonical E2EE production evidence remains open.
rows.test_evidence: temporary-key destroy; invalid peer key; encrypt/decrypt round-trip/failure; participant add/remove; block ordering/replay; reconnect/subchain retry; failure terminality; emoji verification changes; teardown/account-call switch; media prefix encryption boundary.
rows.reachability_status: accepted-tree exact blob responsibility proven; canonical closure open
rows.notes: Transport security is not a substitute for this end-to-end call responsibility.
